result.title: Leakage-Controlled Structure-Preserving Augmentation and Template-Aware Evaluation for Bangla Symptom-Based Disease Prediction
result.summary: Bangla symptom-based disease prediction is commonly evaluated on a small, imbalanced structured benchmark containing many profiles that differ by only one or two symptoms. We test whether train-only asymmetric Bernoulli perturbation improves classification using 725 unique profiles spanning 85 diseases and 172 binary symptoms. Experiments use ten repeated real-profile holdouts and parent-grouped inner cross-validation. The 2 x 2 design separates augmentation from hyperparameter tuning, with exact duplication, random oversampling, class weighting, and SMOTEN as balancing controls. For Bernoulli Naive Bayes (BNB), the gain over tuned raw training does not withstand Holm correction, although BNB attains the highest mean accuracy (97.50%). The boosted-tree models benefit substantially: XGBoost, LightGBM, and CatBoost improve by 18.10, 28.45, and 10.09 percentage points, respectively. A Hamming-distance audit places 91.0% of standard held-out profiles within one symptom bit of the training data. Accuracy decreases on a same-disease 1-bit-purged challenge; nevertheless, XGBoost and LightGBM retain large augmentation gains. We also evaluate robustness to missing and spurious symptoms and the faithfulness of BNB explanations. Overall, Bernoulli perturbation is useful for some model families, but benchmark accuracy should be interpreted together with template proximity.

AI.brief_summary: 论文在 725 个孟加拉语症状档案（85 类疾病、172 个二值症状）上检验仅基于训练集的不对称 Bernoulli 扰动增强，采用重复真实档案留出与父组内层交叉验证，并辅以 Hamming 距离泄漏审计、1-bit 剔除挑战集及缺失/虚假症状鲁棒性和解释忠实度评估。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「模板邻近」泄漏审计与删除/添加症状的扰动评测，可能为 LVR 中视觉证据筛选、捷径泄漏及证据缺失下的评价设计提供核查线索，但领域与方法均相距较远。
